actions.body: Investigation into rational agency reveals that intelligent systems often face unrecognized limitations when bridging the gap between planning and execution. Recent evidence [source-e8ebac5ba0244992] emphasizes that solution plan execution is a critical, yet often neglected, component of agent capability. Our review of cognitive architectures [source-c6430c5161404598] indicates that many frameworks struggle with performance degradation when metareasoning overhead increases. We maintain that distinguishing between these two phases is essential for detecting system-level blind spots. Future work will continue to probe whether these limitations are intrinsic to architectural design or artifacts of specific problem formulations.
actions.lede: Rational agency requires not just the formulation of a solution plan, but its effective execution—a distinction often obscured in simplified cognitive models.
actions.reason: Synthesize accumulated findings on reasoning limits and agent architecture to address the commitment.
actions.title: Planning vs. Execution: Limits in Agentic Reasoning
